# 18. Analytics

<!-- Generated by tools/build_checklists.py. Edit the generator to change checklist structure. -->

**Purpose:** Measure useful outcomes with privacy-aware, free-tier-friendly analytics that do not compromise performance or user trust.

## Universal Constraints
- [ ] The solution must remain static front-end only: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, images, fonts, documents, and generated static files only.
- [ ] The stack must avoid proprietary lock-in, paid builders, paid plugins, closed hosting features that cannot be replaced, and opaque third-party scripts where an open or free-tier-friendly alternative exists.
- [ ] Every decision must be documented as a quality rule, acceptance criterion, or exception with rationale; implementation notes belong outside the checklist.
- [ ] Every checklist item must be testable by review, automated audit, source inspection, browser testing, or client sign-off.
- [ ] Manual exceptions must record the owner, reason, expiration date, affected pages, and residual risk.

## Must Exist
- [ ] An analytics measurement plan tied to business goals and user journeys.
- [ ] A tool decision record comparing free or open-source options such as server logs, self-hosted analytics, Plausible Community Edition, Matomo, Umami, GoatCounter, or privacy-friendly free tiers.
- [ ] A consent model for jurisdictions where analytics storage or identifiers require consent.
- [ ] A pageview definition and event naming convention.
- [ ] A conversion event list for calls, emails, forms, downloads, bookings, newsletter signups, portfolio clicks, and local actions.
- [ ] A data minimization policy banning personal data in URLs, event names, event properties, and analytics dashboards.
- [ ] An internal traffic exclusion plan that does not depend on paid analytics features.
- [ ] A reporting cadence and owner for reviewing analytics after launch.

## Must Be True
- [ ] Analytics must answer decisions the business will actually make.
- [ ] Tracking must not load before consent where consent is required.
- [ ] Analytics code must be replaceable and documented.
- [ ] Events must be stable across pages and releases.
- [ ] Analytics must not collect form message content, names, emails, phone numbers, or other personal data unless legally reviewed and necessary.
- [ ] The site must remain functional when analytics scripts are blocked.
- [ ] Analytics must not materially harm Core Web Vitals.
- [ ] Reports must separate quality signals from vanity metrics.

## Must Be Checked
- [ ] Check that page views fire once per page load and use production URLs.
- [ ] Check that conversion events fire only on meaningful actions or successful submissions where possible.
- [ ] Check consent accept, reject, revoke, and default states.
- [ ] Check that outbound links, downloads, tel links, mailto links, and form submissions are tracked consistently.
- [ ] Check that query strings with personal data are stripped or avoided.
- [ ] Check that analytics script failures do not throw visible errors.
- [ ] Check that privacy policy describes the analytics tool, purpose, retention, and opt-out where applicable.
- [ ] Check that dashboard access follows least privilege.

## Must Be Avoided
- [ ] Avoid installing multiple analytics platforms without a specific reason.
- [ ] Avoid collecting personal data by accident through event labels or URLs.
- [ ] Avoid heatmaps, session replay, or fingerprinting without strict legal review and consent.
- [ ] Avoid marketing tags that fire before consent.
- [ ] Avoid treating analytics setup as complete before production verification.
- [ ] Avoid paid-only analytics dependencies for core measurement.

## Premium Acceptance Standard
- [ ] Analytics must be simple enough to maintain and accurate enough to trust.
- [ ] The measurement plan must distinguish traffic, engagement, conversion, and lead quality.
- [ ] Privacy and performance must be first-class analytics requirements.
- [ ] The client must understand what is measured and what is intentionally not measured.

## Automation Hooks
- [ ] Use generated consent-aware analytics loader templates when tracking is required.
- [ ] Use audits to detect common analytics scripts, missing consent hooks, and personal-data-prone URL patterns.

## Detailed Best-Practice Review Areas
- [ ] Analytics strategy answers where visitors come from, which pages attract/lose visitors, which pages create leads, which CTAs/forms/contact methods work, which devices/sources convert, and which content supports conversion.
- [ ] Tools must be free/open-source-friendly, static-compatible, lightweight, privacy-conscious, exportable, removable, and not duplicated.
- [ ] Privacy-first analytics avoids personal/sensitive/form-field data, prefers cookie-free where possible, respects consent, uses reasonable retention, limits access, and matches the privacy policy.
- [ ] Page views, traffic sources, conversions, CTA clicks, forms, contact clicks, scroll/engagement, blog/content, portfolio/case study, multilingual, static product/payment links, 404/errors, event naming, dashboard, reports, consent/compliance, performance impact, internal traffic, UTM/campaigns, SEO analytics, UX analytics, heatmaps/session recording, A/B testing, free stack, hosting metrics, data quality, launch QA, maintenance, what not to track, best metrics, and final approval are checked.
- [ ] Reports separate traffic from leads, primary from secondary conversions, clicks from confirmed submissions, and useful action from vanity metrics.

## Report Output Required
- [ ] Report every failed automated check with severity, checklist category, issue code, affected file or page, evidence, whether it is script-fixable, and how to fix it.
- [ ] Report every manual-only failure with reviewer, affected page or component, expected standard, actual behavior, recommended fix, owner, and target date.
- [ ] Separate launch blockers from quality improvements so critical static-site failures cannot be hidden by low-priority polish notes.
- [ ] Attach the JSON audit report, Markdown audit report, screenshots where visual proof is needed, and manual QA evidence for browser, device, keyboard, screen reader, form, analytics, and live deployment checks.

## Evidence Required
- [ ] Record reviewed pages, tools used, dates, reviewers, unresolved exceptions, and links to generated reports.
- [ ] Attach screenshots or source references for failures that cannot be proven by automated reports.
- [ ] Mark checklist items as complete only when the production static output satisfies the rule.
